<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>Session resume review</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="demistify/theme.css">
<script type="module" src="demistify/runtime.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
<ex-document>
# Session resume review

“Resume sessions after socket drops” · Review date: 2026-10-14 · Illustrative change

<ex-grid cols="3">
<ex-callout id="verdict" title="Request changes" tone="risk" span="2">
The change fixes resume after network blips but breaks resume after every deploy: sessions live only in process memory. Two blocking findings must be resolved: restart durability (F1) and expired sessions still attaching (F2).

Fix F2 in this change, decide the F1 storage option, and answer F5 before merge. Reviewers recommend Redis for F1.
</ex-callout>
<ex-stat value="0%" label="Resume after deploy" note="After this change; 12% before. Supplied staging soak result." tone="risk"></ex-stat>
</ex-grid>

<ex-route label="Review in 60 seconds">
<ex-step to="verdict">Read the merge verdict.</ex-step>
<ex-step to="f1" open="sidebar">See why every restart loses resumability.</ex-step>
<ex-step to="f2" open="sidebar">Inspect the expired-session fallthrough.</ex-step>
<ex-step to="redis">Review the recommended fix and its cost.</ex-step>
<ex-step to="evidence">Compare the supplied soak results.</ex-step>
</ex-route>

## Exact change and findings

The displayed diff counts every row, including removed rows: function at 40, removed rows 41–42, additions 43–48, closing brace at 49. Findings use these displayed line numbers.

<ex-grid cols="3">
<ex-code id="resume-diff" title="src/session/resume.ts · displayed lines 40–49" lang="diff" start="40" span="2">
<script type="text/plain">
@@ -40,7 +40,12 @@ export function resume(id: string)
 export function resume(id: string): Session | undefined {
-  const socket = sockets.get(id);
-  return socket?.session;
+  const session = registry.get(id);
+  if (!session) return undefined;
+  if (session.expiresAt < Date.now()) {
+    registry.delete(id);
+  }
+  return session.attach(currentSocket());
 }
</script>
<ex-note line="43" tone="risk">F1 · blocking: the in-memory Map is empty after any deploy or crash; every resume misses.</ex-note>
<ex-note line="44" tone="question">F3 · nit: log the session id at debug level so silent misses become visible in traces.</ex-note>
<ex-note line="45" tone="risk">F2 · blocking, lines 45–47: deleting the expired session does not stop execution; line 48 still attaches it. Return undefined after deleting.</ex-note>
<ex-note line="48" tone="note">F4 · nice: attach centralizes the socket swap, previously scattered across two call sites.</ex-note>
</ex-code>
<ex-card id="f1" title="F1 · Restart erases the registry" tone="risk" icon="database" tag="blocking · resume.ts:43" sticky>
`registry` is an in-memory Map. After any deploy or crash it is empty, so every resume returns `undefined` and clients start new sessions.

The lookup survives socket loss only while the process survives. F1 needs a durability decision; Redis is the reviewers’ recommendation.
</ex-card>
</ex-grid>

<ex-grid cols="2">
<ex-card id="f2" title="F2 · Expired session still attaches" tone="risk" icon="bug" tag="blocking · resume.ts:45–47">
The expiry branch deletes the session but falls through to `session.attach(currentSocket())` on line 48. The local session reference still exists after the Map entry is deleted.

**Required fix:** return `undefined` immediately after deleting the expired session.
</ex-card>
<ex-card id="f3" title="F3 · Make resume misses visible" tone="question" icon="file" tag="nit · resume.ts:44">
The early return drops the miss silently. Log the session id at debug level so resume misses are visible in traces.
</ex-card>
<ex-card id="f4" title="F4 · One owner for socket swapping" tone="note" icon="plug" tag="nice · resume.ts:48">
`attach` keeps the socket swap in one place. The old code scattered it across two call sites.
</ex-card>
<ex-card id="f5" title="F5 · Who controls the grace window?" tone="question" icon="clock" tag="question · registry.ts">
Is the 5-minute grace window configurable per tenant, or fixed? Answer before merge. No line number was supplied for this finding.
</ex-card>
</ex-grid>

## Reconnect flow

The intended flow has four participants: Client, Gateway, Registry and Session. The expired-session path below describes the required behavior; F2 means the current diff does not yet implement it.

<ex-grid cols="3">
<ex-mermaid id="reconnect-flow" span="2">
<script type="text/plain">
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway
    participant Registry
    participant Session
    Client->>Gateway: Reconnect with session id
    Gateway->>Gateway: resume(id)
    Gateway->>Registry: Look up session id
    Registry-->>Gateway: Session or missing
    alt Found and not expired
        Gateway->>Session: attach(new socket)
        Session-->>Gateway: Attached session
        Gateway-->>Client: Confirm resumed session
    else Missing or expired
        Gateway-->>Client: Start a new session
    end
</script>
</ex-mermaid>
<ex-callout title="Where the implementation diverges" tone="risk" sticky>
A missing entry already returns `undefined`. An expired entry is deleted but still attached, so it does not reach the intended “start a new session” outcome.

After a restart, all entries are missing. No reconnect can reach the successful branch until the registry is durable.
</ex-callout>
</ex-grid>

## Repository changes

<ex-tree id="repository-changes" title="Files touched" icon="folder">
- src/
  - session/
    - changed: [resume.ts — lookup and attach diff](#resume-diff)
    - added: [registry.ts — 64 lines; grace-window question](#f5)
    - changed: socket.ts
    - removed: legacy-store.ts
- test/
  - session/
    - added: resume.test.ts
</ex-tree>

The supplied brief identifies these files; it does not include the contents of the registry, socket implementation, deleted store or new tests. Their correctness and test coverage are not independently established here.

## Fix options for F1

<ex-grid cols="3" swipe>
<ex-card id="memory" title="In-memory registry" tone="risk" icon="cpu" tag="current">
Fast and simple. Loses every session on restart.

**Tradeoff:** speed over durability. The current option cannot satisfy resume across deploys or crashes.
</ex-card>
<ex-card id="redis" title="Redis-backed registry" tone="decision" icon="database" tag="recommended" pick>
Survives restarts and is shared across instances. Adds Redis to every environment and about **2 ms per resume**.

**Tradeoff:** durability for a dependency. Reviewers recommend this option; the prototype results below support the recommendation, but do not establish a production rollout.
</ex-card>
<ex-card id="sticky-sockets" title="Sticky sockets at the load balancer" tone="risk" icon="cloud" tag="alternative">
No new state. Breaks whenever an instance is replaced, so it does not fix deploys.

**Tradeoff:** no new state but fragile. Routing affinity cannot preserve the state of a replaced instance.
</ex-card>
</ex-grid>

## Evidence

<ex-callout id="evidence" title="Network recovery improves; restart recovery remains broken" tone="tldr">
The supplied staging soak test reports resume success as a percentage of reconnects. This change improves network blips from 35% to 98%, while deploy recovery falls from 12% to 0%. The Redis prototype reports 96% after deploy and 94% after an instance crash.

| Scenario | Before | After this change | With Redis registry (prototype) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Network blip | 35% | 98% | 98% |
| Deploy | 12% | 0% | 96% |
| Instance crash | 0% | 0% | 94% |

These are figures supplied in the illustrative brief, not measurements run for this explainer. Sample sizes, test methodology and variability were not supplied. The approximately 2 ms Redis cost is also a supplied claim, with no timing evidence included.
</ex-callout>

## Next steps before merge

<ex-tree id="next-steps" title="Author and reviewer checklist" icon="git-branch">
- [ ] [Fix F2 in this change: return undefined after deleting an expired session](#f2)
- [ ] [Decide the F1 option: reviewers recommend Redis](#redis)
- [ ] [Answer F5: tenant configuration or a fixed 5-minute grace window?](#f5)
</ex-tree>

The review remains **request changes**. F3 is a nit and F4 is positive feedback; neither closes the two blocking findings.
</ex-document>
</body>
</html>
